new_entry_when: When is this entry for? A day can hold more than one entry.
entry_nudges_sub: Suggest adding details after a mood-only save.
note_placeholder: What happened? How did it feel?
gender_hint: However it feels right now. There are no wrong answers.
body_map_hint: Optional. Pick a spot on the body and how intense it feels right now.
delete_entry_hint: The entry and its photos will be removed. This cannot be undone.
streak_with_entry: days in a row with an entry
backup_stale_title: Your last backup was {days} days ago
backup_stale_body: Your journal lives only on this device.
empty_home_title: Your story starts with one entry
empty_home_body: Log how today felt. A mood is enough, and you can add more later.
home_milestones_empty_body: Add a coming-out date, a start date, or anything else worth marking.
metric_note: The same colour choice drives the calendar heat-map.
heat_hint: Days with entries are filled in: deeper colour means a higher {metric}. Days with several entries show the day’s average. Tap a filled day to see its entries.
add_another_entry: Add another entry for this day
nothing_logged_body: You can still add an entry for it. Memory counts.
search_hint: Notes and tags, with or without diacritics. “lozko” finds “łóżko”.
no_results_body: No entries match “{query}”. Try a shorter word: prefixes match too.
search_no_results_filtered: No entries match these filters yet.
not_enough_data: Not enough data in this range yet.
insights_note: Observations, not conclusions. Tags with fewer than 3 entries in range are hidden.
insights_empty: Not enough tagged entries in this range yet.
recap_sub: a look back at last month
body_map_sub: track one spot's intensity over time
a11y_legibility_boost_sub: stronger secondary text and clearer separators
a11y_motion_reduce_override_sub: keeps animations reduced even if the system allows motion
preset_note: Chooses which scales appear when you log. Past values are never lost when you switch.
custom_dimension_sub: your own words at both ends
tag_groups_sub: choose which groups appear on entries
body_measurements_sub: waist, hips, chest and underbust over time
tagdesc_dt_physical: Discomfort with your body's shape or sex characteristics.
tagdesc_dt_biochemical: A mismatch between the hormones your body produces and what your brain expects.
tagdesc_dt_social: Discomfort with how other people perceive you and address you.
tagdesc_dt_societal: Discomfort with gendered roles and expectations built into society, not any one interaction.
tagdesc_dt_sexual: Discomfort with sexual roles or expectations that don't fit how you experience your gender.
tagdesc_dt_presentational: Discomfort with how you present, or are made to present, through clothing, hair and other visible choices.
tagdesc_dt_existential: Grief over experiences and milestones missed while growing up as a gender that wasn't yours.
not_in_preset: Not in the current preset, kept from this entry
empty_entry: Add a mood, a value, a tag, a note or a photo first
ob_welcome_body: A private diary for your transition: moods, gender feelings, milestones, photos. All of it stays on this device. No account, no cloud, no tracking.
ob_name_title: What should the app call you?
ob_name_body: Only used to greet you. It never leaves this device, and you can skip it.
ob_track_title: How do you want to track gender?
ob_track_body: A preset chooses which scales appear when you log. You can change or customise this any time in Settings.
ob_milestone_body: A day that matters, past or future. Anniversaries come back each year, and future dates count down.
ob_lock_body: A PIN keeps curious eyes out if someone picks up your phone. It is a lock on the app, not the encryption secret: that secret is either your journal passphrase or a key kept on this device, and you can add or change the passphrase later in Settings. Biometrics can come later.
ob_done_body: Everything you write stays here, with you. One short entry a day is plenty.
pin_setup_body: Four digits, asked for every time the app opens. It keeps the app shut to a casual look, and it is not what encrypts your journal. Forget it and the only way back in is to reset the app and lose what is on here, so pick one you will remember.
pin_confirm_body: The same four digits again, so a slip of the thumb doesn’t lock you out.
pin_unlock_body: Enter your PIN to open your journal.
pin_mismatch: Those two did not match. Start again.
pin_throttled: Too many wrong tries. Try again in {seconds}s.
pin_forgot_no_recovery: There is no way to recover it
pin_forgot_hash_note: The PIN is stored as a hash, so nobody, including this app, can read it back.
reset_offer: You can start over instead. That deletes every entry, photo and setting on this device and takes you back to the welcome screen. If you have an archive from an earlier export, you can restore from it afterwards.
reset_offer_archive_password: You can start over instead. That deletes every entry, photo and setting on this device and takes you back to the welcome screen. If you have an archive from an earlier export, you can restore from it afterwards with that archive’s own password.
reset_failed: Could not reset the app. Try again, or close and reopen it first.
lock_auto_note: Locks automatically when the app goes to background.
pp_setup_body: This passphrase becomes the portable secret for this journal. After the session ends, you will need it to open the journal again. Save it in a password manager now: Gender Diary has no account behind it and cannot recover the passphrase or the journal if it is lost.
pp_unlock_body: Enter your journal passphrase to decrypt your journal.
pp_mode_passphrase: Passphrase mode: you type a journal passphrase after the session ends. It is the only portable secret.
pp_mode_device: Skip for now: this journal stays tied to this browser or device profile. There is no passphrase prompt, but losing the profile, device or local key can make this copy unreadable.
pp_mode_pin: App lock PIN: a separate casual-access layer. It is not the journal secret.
pp_skip_body: Gender Diary can keep this journal behind a local key saved only in this browser or on this device. That means no typed passphrase on a cold start, but this copy is more tightly tied to this installation.
pp_skip_ack: I understand that without a journal passphrase, losing this browser profile, device or local key may make this journal unrecoverable, and Gender Diary cannot recover secrets for me.
pp_skip_no_device_lock: Skip mode needs a device screen lock before Android can bind the journal key to this phone. Set one first, or choose a journal passphrase now.
pp_skip_unavailable: This browser could not keep a device-bound journal key. Choose a journal passphrase instead.
pp_forgot_no_recovery: There is no way to recover it
pp_forgot_key_note: The journal is encrypted with a key only your passphrase can unwrap. Nobody, including this app, can read it back without one or the other.
pp_convert_setup_body: Your journal is on this device but it is not encrypted yet. Choosing a passphrase now encrypts every entry, photo and setting already in it, and from then on this passphrase is the only thing that opens them. Save it in a password manager before you continue: Gender Diary has no account behind it and cannot recover the passphrase or the journal if it is lost.
pp_convert_resume_body: Encrypting your journal was interrupted. Enter the passphrase you chose and it will carry on from where it stopped. Everything you had written is still here.
pp_converting_note: This can take a while on a big journal. If it stops, opening Gender Diary again picks up where it left off.
pp_converting_database: Copying your journal into encrypted storage…
pp_convert_refused_space: Encrypting your journal means writing a second copy of it before the first one goes, and there is not enough room on this device: it needs about {need} free and has {free}. Free some space and open Gender Diary again. Nothing has been changed.
pp_convert_refused_schema: This journal was last opened by a newer version of Gender Diary, and this one would not understand all of it. Update the app, then open it again. Nothing has been changed.
pp_add_body: Right now this journal is tied to this browser or device. Adding a passphrase wraps the same journal key under a portable secret, so the journal itself is not rewritten. After that, you will need the passphrase to open this journal after the session ends.
pp_change_body: The passphrase wraps the key your journal is encrypted with, so changing it takes effect immediately and nothing is re-encrypted. The old passphrase stops working everywhere, including for this device’s unlock screen. Gender Diary cannot recover a lost passphrase, so save the new one in a password manager before you change it.
pp_change_mismatch: The new passphrase and its confirmation did not match.
pp_added_toast: Passphrase added. Save it in your password manager.
dbr_title: This journal was tied to this device
dbr_body: This journal was opened without a journal passphrase, and the local key this browser or device kept for it is no longer available. Gender Diary cannot recover that key, so this copy cannot be reopened.
pp_change_wrong_current: The current passphrase is not right.
pp_changed_toast: Passphrase changed. Update it in your password manager too.
ak_unlock_body: Your journal is encrypted. Android is holding the key and hands it over once it knows it is you.
ak_prompt_subtitle: Unlock to decrypt what you have written.
ak_locked_out: Too many tries. The sensor will not take another one for a while, but your device PIN still will.
ak_unavailable: This device has no fingerprint or face check that Gender Diary can use.
ak_unenrolled: There is no fingerprint or face set up on this device.
ak_no_lock_body: Your journal’s key lives in Android’s key store, and Android will not hold a key on a device with no screen lock. Set a PIN, pattern or password in the device settings, then come back here.
ak_forgot_key_note: The journal is encrypted with a key Android holds for you and unwraps for nobody else. Without it, nothing can read the journal back, this app included.
ak_invalidated_body: Android destroys the key it was holding for you when a device’s screen lock is removed, and there is no way to bring it back. Your entries are still on this phone and nothing can open them any more. If you have an archive from an earlier export, you can start over and restore from it.
ak_plaintext_journal: This phone still has a journal from before Android encryption. Install the conversion build first, then come back to this one.
boot_no_persistent_storage: This browser didn’t grant persistent storage. Export backups regularly so nothing is lost to storage pressure.
update_ready_body: Switching to it reloads the app. Nothing you have written is lost, and there is no hurry.
boot_schema_too_new_title: Your journal is newer than this version
boot_schema_too_new_body: A newer version of Gender Diary has already opened this journal, and this build would not understand all of it, so it has not touched it. Nothing has been changed and nothing is lost. What opens it again is that newer version, and the button below goes and looks for it.
boot_schema_too_new_still_old: Still nothing newer on offer here. Your journal is untouched, so this is worth trying again later.
boot_restore_offer: Your journal from before this update is still on this device. Putting it back replaces what the update left half finished, so anything the app has written since the copy was taken goes with it, and that cannot be undone. If this version still cannot open the restored journal, the version you had before can.
boot_restore_failed: That did not work. The copy is still on the device.
exp_last_backup_never: never, so your journal exists only on this device
exp_encrypted_body: Everything, including entries, photos, milestones, tags, your own scales and presets, lab results and settings, packed into one file and encrypted before it leaves the app.
exp_crypto_note: AES-256-GCM, key derived with Argon2id. Without the password the file is unreadable, including to the person who wrote this app.
exp_cancelled: Export cancelled. Nothing left the app.
exp_failed: The export could not be finished. Nothing was saved.
exp_auto_sub: encrypted backup to a folder you pick
exp_auto_note: Folder: {folder}. Backups are encrypted with your export password, and that password is never stored.
exp_auto_password_saved: Export password is saved securely on this device for scheduled backups.
exp_auto_password_missing: No password saved yet for scheduled backups.
exp_auto_reselect_needed: Backup folder access was lost. Pick a folder again.
imp_password_placeholder: The password it was exported with
imp_merge_note: Anything the backup has and this device doesn’t is added. Nothing you already logged is changed.
imp_replace_note: Everything in this journal is discarded and the backup takes its place. Your PIN, app lock and disguise settings stay as they are.
imp_password_needed: Type the password this backup was made with.
imp_replaced_toast: Restored. This journal is the backup now.
imp_merged_toast: Merged in. Nothing you already had was touched.
imp_wrong_password: That password doesn’t unlock this file. Passwords are case-sensitive, so check and try again. Nothing was imported.
imp_not_an_archive: This isn’t a Gender Diary backup file. Nothing was imported.
imp_newer_version: This backup was made by a newer version of the app. Update first, then import it. Nothing was imported.
imp_corrupt: This file is damaged and can’t be read to the end. Nothing was imported; your journal is exactly as it was.
imp_failed: The import couldn’t be finished. Your journal is exactly as it was.
plain_body: For spreadsheets and portability: CSV (flat) or JSON (full structure).
exp_warning_title: There’s no way to recover a forgotten password
exp_warning_body: If you forget this password, the archive is unreadable forever, including to the person who wrote this app. There is no recovery option, no exceptions.
plain_notice_body: Anyone who gets it can read your whole journal. Store it somewhere only you can reach, or use the encrypted export instead.
daylio_row_sub: moods, activities and notes, always a merge
daylio_unmapped: These mood labels aren’t mapped: {labels}. Nothing has been imported. Rename them in Daylio to a default English or Polish mood, export again, and retry.
daylio_unreadable: This CSV couldn’t be read. Nothing has been imported.
daylio_failed: The Daylio import couldn’t be finished. Your journal is exactly as it was.
daylio_always_merge: This import is always a merge. Nothing you already logged is changed.
mood_colours_note: Kept separate from the palette above, so a mood dot never looks like a gender colour.
settings_passphrase_sub_portable: portable secret enabled · change it here
settings_passphrase_sub_device: device-bound right now · add a portable secret here
security_intro: Your passphrase unlocks your journal's encryption. Without it, nobody gets back in, not even the app. PIN and biometrics are a faster lock for a casual glance, and losing them costs you a reset, never your data.
bio_row_sub: faster unlock with a fingerprint or face
bio_row_needs_surface: needs the PIN lock or device-bound mode
bio_ask_boot_body: Your device's own lock opens your journal every time the app starts, whichever lock that is for you. Saying yes opens it the moment you arrive. Saying no leaves the same lock behind a button you tap first.
bio_ask_pin_body: Your fingerprint or face can unlock the app as fast as your PIN. Turn it off any time in Security settings, and your PIN always still works.
about_license: Free software under the GPLv3 license. The source code is public.
about_no_network_title: This app makes no network requests.
about_no_network_body: No account, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics. Your journal exists only on this device and in backups you export yourself.
disguise_app_sub_android: the launcher icon and name become a neutral “Notes”, and the app closes briefly to switch
disguise_app_sub_web: the browser tab shows a neutral “Notes” title and icon, and the app installs under that name
disguise_preview_android: how the app appears in your launcher
disguise_installed_note: If you have already installed this app, the name and icon on your home screen change when your browser next refreshes them. Browsers do that on their own schedule, so it may take a while.
lock_on_leave_sub: locks the moment the app goes to background
quick_exit_sub_web: two-finger swipe down blanks the tab and locks instantly
quick_exit_no_lock: without app lock it only blanks the screen
ms_intro: Days that matter. Past ones come back as anniversaries, and future ones count down on Home.
ms_delete_hint: Its photo is removed too. This cannot be undone.
tags_intro: Built-in tags can be hidden and their history stays. Your own tags can be renamed or deleted.
tags_delete_hint: This removes the tag from every entry that uses it. The entries themselves are untouched. This cannot be undone.
cd_intro: Track anything the built-in scales miss. You choose the words for both ends.
cd_preview_note: This is how it will look on the entry screen.
cd_added_toast: Scale added to a new custom preset.
labs_intro: Your numbers, your trend. The app never interprets them and gives no medical advice.
labs_too_little: Two results make a trend. Add another when it comes in.
labs_empty_body: Add bloodwork as it comes in and watch your own trend over time. No ranges, no grades, just your numbers.
labs_new_unit_toast: {unit} is new for {analyte}, so it gets its own trend.
labs_no_unit_toast: This result has no unit, so it gets its own trend.
labs_ocr_pick_intro: Pick a photo from gallery or camera. OCR runs on this device.
labs_ocr_permission_denied: Camera or gallery permission was denied. Grant access and try again.
labs_ocr_no_rows_body: OCR found no usable lab rows. Add manually or try another photo.
labs_ocr_review_intro: Check every row before saving. You can edit analyte, value, unit, date and note.
labs_ocr_low_confidence: Low confidence: please double-check this row.
labs_ocr_missing_analyte: Every included row needs an analyte.
labs_ocr_invalid_value: Every included row needs a valid numeric value.
labs_ocr_missing_date: Every included row needs a date before save.
labs_ocr_invalid_date: One of the included dates is invalid.
labs_ocr_failed: OCR import failed. Try another photo.
labs_preferred_units_intro: Pick one default unit per analyte. Existing results stay as logged.
measurements_intro: Your own numbers, logged in whatever unit you measure in. No BMI, no body-composition guesses - just what you tracked.
measurement_too_little: Two measurements make a trend. Add another when you have one.
measurement_empty_body: Log a waist, hip, chest or underbust measurement and watch your own trend over time.
measurement_protocol_waist: Measure at the narrowest point, usually just above the navel. Same time of day and similar tension on the tape make measurements easier to compare - neither is required.
measurement_protocol_hips: Measure around the widest part of the hips and buttocks, with the tape level all the way round.
measurement_protocol_chest: Measure around the fullest part of the chest or bust, with the tape level and not pulled tight.
measurement_protocol_underbust: Measure directly under the bust, where a bra band sits, with the tape snug but not compressing.
labs_context_none: No dosing context was recorded for this draw.
labs_context_needs_time: An hours-since-dose figure needs the draw time. Day-of-interval, for injections, does not.
labs_context_frozen: Recorded when this result was saved, from the dose log as it stood then. Editing a dose later does not change it.
labs_mixed_body: These readings were not all taken under the same conditions:
labs_mixed_position: different points in the dosing interval
regimen_row_sub: What you're taking, and since when
regimen_intro: What you're taking, at what dose and by what route, as it's changed over time. Every entry, photo and lab result is attributed to whichever episode was in effect when it was logged.
regimen_empty_body: Add your current regimen, then log a new episode whenever it changes.
doses_row_sub: Every dose, and how it sits against the schedule
doses_intro: Each dose is filed under whichever regimen episode was in effect when it was taken. Correct a dose's date and it moves to the episode that really covered it.
doses_empty_body: Log a dose and it shows up here, under the regimen episode that was in effect that day.
doses_no_episode: No regimen episode covers this date
dose_time_hint: The time of day is kept, not just the date. Later screens work out how long ago a dose was.
dose_injection_site_hint: Tap where it went. The map marks where the last one went, so you can see what to rotate to.
dose_scheduled_hint: Kept beside what you actually took, so the two can be read side by side later.
adherence_no_episode: There is no regimen episode yet, so there is no schedule to compare against.
adherence_no_schedule: {drug} has no schedule yet. Add one on the regimen screen and the expected doses show up here.
adherence_for_episode: Expected doses for {drug}, counted from its start date.
adherence_paused_note: No dose is expected during a pause, so those days are left out of the list above.
adherence_unmatched_note: Doses with no slot to sit in, either taken during a pause or beyond what the schedule expects.
regimen_schedule_hint: How often this episode expects a dose. Slots are counted from its start date, so editing this does not shift them.
regimen_pauses_hint: A range during which no dose is expected, so a break does not read as a run of missed doses.
regimen_pause_end_hint: Leave empty if the pause is still going.
regimen_stock_link_sub: How much is left, and when it's projected to run out
regimen_exposure_link_sub: Dose totals, days on each route, time on each regimen
stock_intro: How much is left of each drug, and when it's due to run out, both worked out from what you've logged.
stock_empty_body: Record how much you have of a drug, and this screen works out how long it will last from what you log.
stock_run_out_now: Already out, based on what you've logged
stock_run_out_unknown: Not enough dose data yet to project a run-out
exposure_intro: Plain totals from your dose log and regimen history. No target ranges, no comparisons - just what you've logged.
exposure_dose_totals_empty: No doses logged in this range.
exposure_route_days_empty: No regimen history in this range.
exposure_regimen_days_empty: No regimen history in this range.
side_effects_intro: A plain record of what you notice. No grading, no advice - just something to look back on.
side_effect_empty_body: Log a side effect when you notice one. No grading, no advice - just your own record.
effects_timeline_sub: when you first noticed each change
effects_intro: Mark the day you first noticed each change. The shaded bands show what the literature reports as typical timing since your regimen began - a description of what the research says, not a judgement of how fast you're changing.
effects_source: Source: the Endocrine Society's 2017 clinical practice guideline (Hembree et al.), its table of typical timing.
effects_no_regimen_body: This timeline anchors against the day your regimen began. Log a regimen episode first, and it'll pick it up from there.
effect_clear_hint: You can mark it again any time.
effect_window_bounded: The literature reports this usually starts {onsetMin} to {onsetMax} months in, with the full change typically in place by {compMin} to {compMax} months.
effect_window_no_completion: The literature reports this usually starts {onsetMin} to {onsetMax} months in; it doesn't say how long the change takes to finish.
effect_window_open_completion: The literature reports this usually starts {onsetMin} to {onsetMax} months in, and for some people keeps changing past {compMin} months.
hair_intro: Stage yourself against the published Norwood-Hamilton scale whenever you like, and take the same fixed-position photo every few weeks to see how it's going.
hair_unanchored_note: Not anchored to a timeline yet. Log a finasteride, dutasteride or minoxidil dose and staging and photos here will start counting from it.
hair_stage_empty_body: Compare yourself against the published scale and log where you are today.
hair_photo_due_body: It's been a while since the last one. Taking one now keeps the interval even.
hair_photo_protocol_body: Use the same framing, lighting and distance each time, so what changes between photos is your hair and nothing else.
hair_photo_empty_body: Fixed-position photos land here as you take them, oldest first.
ph_compare_reset: One selected photo is no longer available. Pick two anchors again.
ph_pick_two: Every photo in your journal, oldest first. Select two to compare.
ph_one_selected: One selected. Pick a second to compare.
ph_empty_body: Photos you attach to entries and milestones gather here, and one day “then vs now” will be worth it.
photo_heic: This looks like a HEIC photo, which this app can’t read yet. Convert it to JPEG first, or set your camera to save photos as JPEG.
photo_not_an_image: This file isn’t an image this app can read. Try a JPEG or PNG.
rem_web_body: Browsers cannot fire scheduled notifications reliably while the app is closed. Install the Android app to get medication and check-in reminders.
rem_web_note: Your data syncs nowhere, and an encrypted export is how it moves to the Android app safely.
checkin_sub: “How are you today?” · skipped on days you already logged
rem_battery_body: Some phones (Xiaomi, Samsung, Huawei, OnePlus) kill background apps and silence alarms. If reminders stop arriving, allow the app to run in the background.
rem_alarm_note: Exact alarms survive reboots, but aggressive battery savers can silence them.
rem_capabilities_body: Android may block reminder delivery until notifications are allowed, and newer versions can still refuse exact alarms. Reminder and check-in channels live in system notification settings.
rem_hide_titles_sub: notifications show a generic title and message instead of a reminder's name
tl_intro: Your milestones so far, and what’s ahead.
tl_empty_body: Add the days that matter and the shape of your own timeline appears.
home_anniv_years: {name}, {years} ago today. That day mattered. So does this one.
recap_open_month: One month, held in your own words.
recap_open_year: One year, held in your own words.
recap_entries_body: You showed up, again and again. Some days had two entries. Gender moves, and you caught it moving.
recap_entries_quiet_month: A quiet month. Quiet counts too.
recap_entries_quiet_year: A quiet year. Quiet counts too.
recap_mood_body_month: Averaged across the month. It is not a grade, only a record of where you were.
recap_mood_body_year: Averaged across the year. It is not a grade, only a record of where you were.
recap_streak_body: The longest run of days in a row you wrote something down. Consistency is a kindness to your future self.
recap_scale_body_month: The scale that moved furthest this month, first entry to last. Whichever direction it went, it is yours.
recap_scale_body_year: The scale that moved furthest this year, first entry to last. Whichever direction it went, it is yours.
recap_scale_none_month: Not enough logged on any one scale this month to show a shift.
recap_scale_none_year: Not enough logged on any one scale this year to show a shift.
recap_end_body: Thank you for keeping your own record. See you tomorrow.
recap_year_sub: A look back at the year you recorded.
recap_custom_range_required: Pick both start and end days to read this custom range.
recap_open_range: An ongoing window, held in your own words.
recap_entries_quiet_range: A quiet range. Quiet counts too.
recap_mood_body_range: Averaged across this range. It is not a grade, only a record of where you were.
recap_mood_none_range: No moods logged in this range.
recap_ms_none_range: No milestones landed in this range.
recap_scale_body_range: The scale that moved furthest in this range, first entry to last. Whichever direction it went, it is yours.
recap_scale_none_range: Not enough logged on any one scale in this range to show a shift.
recap_change_summary_not_enough: Not enough mood points in this range yet to summarize a change.
wrapped_settings_sub: Look back on a week, a month or a year once it has ended.
wrapped_notify_sub: A notification when a new wrapped is ready, independent of the card above.
wrapped_notification_body: Open the app to look back.
wrapped_off_body: Turn it on in Settings and finished weeks, months and years show up on Home.
wrapped_unknown_body: A wrapped covers a finished week, month or year. Open one from Home.
wrapped_month_intro: One month, as you logged it.
wrapped_year_intro: Twelve months, as you logged them.
wrapped_thin_title: Not much to look back on yet

match.countPlural=one: {count} entry in this period, and a wrapped starts at {floor}.
match.countPlural=other: {count} entries in this period, and a wrapped starts at {floor}.

wrapped_year_close: That was {year}, in your own words.
on_this_day_settings_sub: Look back on a good day from a month, six months or a year ago.
on_this_day_notify_sub: A notification when a good day resurfaces, independent of the card above.
on_this_day_notification_body: Open the app to look back on a good day.
on_this_day_off_body: Turn it on in Settings and a good day from the past can show up on Home again.
on_this_day_home_sub: A good day from your past
on_this_day_none_title: Nothing to look back on today
on_this_day_none_body: On this day only shows a good day from a month, six months or a year ago. None of today's three line up.
retro_notify_capabilities_body: Allow notifications to hear about wrapped and on-this-day. Their channels live in system notification settings.
tally_trend_sub: misgendering and correct gendering, over time
